HF radio can transmit signals over much longer distances, enabling communication with ground stations and other aircraft far away. Overhead maneuver is a series of predetermined maneuvers prescribed for aircraft to enter into the VFR traffic pattern, and to proceed to a landing. It is not an IFR approach procedure. An aircraft executing an overhead maneuver is considered VFR. FR, and the IFR flight plan is canceled when the aircraft reaches the initial point on the initial approach portion of the maneuver. On December 4, 2025, a United Boeing 7 7 7 200, registration November 7 4 0 0 7 performing flight United 9 4 9 from London Heathrow (UK) to San Francisco (USA) with 162 passengers and 12 crew, was enroute at FL3 4 0 over the Atlantic Ocean about 360 nautical miles northwest of Edinburgh (UK) when the crew decided to turn around and divert to Edinburgh due to a burning odour on board. The aircraft landed safely on Edinburgh's Runway 06about one hour after turning around. The airline reported the aircraft diverted to Edinburgh due to a burning smell on board, the passengers were taken to hotels and rebooked onto other flights.

A worker in the airport just finished his work, while he was walking along the apron he found a female pilot was struggling with a huge package. The package was stuck, half of the package was in the plane and another half was out. The worker was a very kind and warmhearted man, so he tried to help the female pilot. He went into the plane and tried his best to push the package, but the package did not move and nothing happened. Later the worker and the pilot decided to push and pull at the same time. They tried so hard over and over again and both got exhausted, but they still couldn't move the package. The worker felt hopeless and he said it was impossible to get the package out of the plane. Then he heard the pilot shrieking, "Oh, no! I was trying to stuff it in!"

One day, an accident happened because an aircraft was guided improperly by a marshaller when parking. The marshaller first guided the aircraft to a gate. When the aircraft was near the stop line, the marshaller gave a premature crossed wands signal which means stopping taxing, so the aircraft was stopped abruptly. The pilot set the parking brake and released the seatbelt sign. Unexpectedly, the marshaller showed the separated wands again and stopped them a little forward of the point. He did not give a clear signal, and the sudden stop caused fatigue and a medical emergency of 2 passengers. When the marshaller was asked about the signal, he said he did not give the signal. Anyway, it was not a good guidance but the final position of the aircraft was proper. Luckily there were no injuries on board.
